title: Position your product against the alternatives
summary: Positioning explains what your product is, who it is for and why it is better than the alternatives. Clear positioning makes marketing, sales and even product decisions easier.

beginner: List what users would use if your product did not exist.
intermediate: Map the real alternatives, including doing nothing.
Identify your unique strengths and the value they create.
Define the users who care most about that value.
Choose the market frame that makes your strengths obvious, and test the wording.
experienced: Revisit positioning as the market changes.
Align product, marketing and sales on one positioning.
Use positioning to say no to features that blur it.

canDelegateTo.task: Write and refine the positioning statement

toolExamples.miro: Map alternatives and your strengths on a board.
toolExamples.google-docs: Keep a positioning canvas with each element and its evidence.
toolExamples.claude: Ask it to rewrite your positioning for three different audiences.

pitfalls: Positioning that product and sales do not share
